This is an implemented control inventory, not a test-run report.
Review on changed standards, mechanisms, evidence or coverage. The
[registry](control-registry.json) owns these mappings; [engineering](engineering.md)
owns mandatory wording and [charter](charter.md) owns principles.

Automatic controls run in the common lane. Runtime controls act in the live system;
their tests cover only the stated cases. Manual controls require the named review
or probe. Implementation and evidence links do not assert a current execution or pass.

## Mechanisms and coverage

### C-PORTABLE — Portable regression lane (automatic)

Controller, HTTP adapter, setup and spectator regressions. Includes gameplay record validation and bounded evidence retention using synthetic observations. Passive planner/skill/supervisor composition, continuation and uncertainty are covered by real-component synthetic fixtures. Explicit --fast checkpoint command compiles Python, runs Ruff correctness diagnostics, Import Linter contracts, JS syntax, markdown-it-py link/image targets, document stewardship, governance and diff whitespace. Relevant focused behavioral tests remain a lead-selected obligation. The default full command additionally renders diagrams, runs all Python tests and delayed-image viewer regressions. Structured player tests cover fixed HTTP transport, stable requests, archive images and SDK framing, not real host behavior. Apply S-CODE whole-loop variation and independently shaped portability-fixture requirements where relevant; tests must demonstrate coverage. Synthetic cases do not qualify native or cross-game behavior.

Owner: maintainer. Trigger: Fast structural checks on each configured local commit; focused tests on affected behavior; full portable checks at coherent integration/formal acceptance and PR/main CI events.
Enforcement: Opt-in project-local pre-commit hook runs --fast. Actions controller job runs full default checks for all PRs and pushes to main; no required-job path filters. GitHub concurrency cancels superseded PR runs only. Main retains strict Actions-app15368 controller requirement under ruleset25346774. Hooks remain bypassable; a fast pass never establishes behavioral/full portable acceptance. Hosted activation evidence is recorded in the issue/PR after the configuration is exercised.
Failure response: Preserve failure output, fix the cause and rerun before claiming portable acceptance.

### C-RUNTIME — Live authority and input guards (runtime)

Single-controller mission dispatch and admission, original typed operation accounting, HTTP trust boundary, historical memory observer and spectator input freshness. One MissionRuntime accepts strict mission/8 through authenticated HTTP and bounded JSON CLI; old mission/2, mission/3, mission/4, mission/5, mission/6 and mission/7 records and Stop-finish flags reject. One writer uses exact controller leases, final source/image preflight, durable intents and original root/child budgets. Controller/native fences reject stale, paused or competing input and retain unknown delivery without replay; admission counters exclude raw-command/Start races while independent Pause remains available. Registered launch retains the fixed child and paused menu. Creation/save/load requires owned transitions, provisional visible identity and canonical all-session adoption before maps, time or native memory facts. Verified normal exit retires only its exact pending input and unused capacity, preserving the unknown ACK. Normal finish uses every owned exit, retained historical source integrity and coherent objective Work as of its exact event; no native input. Its immutable report precedes terminal epoch/deadline checks, and Pause/expiry/crash cannot replay completion. Cached viewer status distinguishes historical memory, process samples, saved exit, reported completion, cleanup and actual mission phase; rendering grants no authority. Quiescent handoff/claim atomically retain actor history without input; bounded current-version successor packets cover unfinished Work. Separate linked readmission charges one Resume under original deadlines and exact source/Pause fences; history restores no consent. Typed item/count/inspection roots and one-observation activity polls share original phase/Work limits. Item quantity editing requires its exact returned count-opening transition; focus never auto-confirms. Trusted activity control captures validated terminal evidence before reconciliation persistence and checks fixed native expiry before publication. Cached SQLite aggregates distinguish retained operation requests and charged primitive dispositions from unmeasured model/tool/intervention costs. The observer separates current private activity from historical results and exposes bounded query-specific memory with explicit truncation/raw context. Known nondelivery retains costs without invalidating memory; freshness, scope and unknown effects still apply. A private unknown-dispatch candidate retains original root/actor/Pause/takeover/capacity custody. One bounded pre-Observe collection retains exact unclaimed retirement or correlated terminal evidence in existing records, without accepting it as current, clearing unknown effects or granting Resume. Delayed I/O cannot admit late evidence; collection misses remain ambiguous. Ledger10 uses one closed 32768-byte typed EffectReconciliation envelope for delivery, lifecycle and owned exit. Write/reopen correlate basis semantics with independent original dispatch receipts, actor/root/Work/epoch, source IDs and collection clocks; old ledger/effect shapes reject. Framed late results consume original reserved capacity before diagnostic Observe. Explicit reconciliation needs current fresh paused evidence and does not rewrite the unknown ACK/charge. Separate normal-play recovery readmission charges one Resume; navigation retains its original goal/Work/root, first game anchor and cumulative limits. Pending continuation fences competing roots/handoff; unknown Resume and unsupported ownership stop. Historical or orphan proof restores no private consent. Aged lifecycle Resume and owned quit confirmation refresh the exact guarded checkpoint inside the operation under original child/root/mission deadlines. Resume records source lineage before a lease exists; typed exit revalidation links the immutable interpretation to the dispatched source at write/reopen and orphan proof checks, requiring exact PNG rather than native-state equivalence. Local malformed lifecycle confirmation returns blocked before dispatch without renewing the original phase; corrected requests retain full source/Pause/image/deadline checks. Premature exact provisional identity inspection returns a correctable zero-input readmission explanation only after complete committed proof, current source/image, ownership, quiescence and original resource checks; no refresh, activation, lease or Resume. Explicit same-root lifecycle readmission revalidates that full paused transition/effect proof before activation and charged Resume; aged feedback grants no freshness. Known game-time exhaustion gates every input lane and revokes authority after settlement; software maximum eight days, default twelve hours, no cleanup exemption. Eligible internally inconsistent skill source metadata returns blocked before refresh, phase mutation or primitive admission only after applicable existing authority/ownership/budget and native-state/image fences; original deadlines and consent remain unchanged. A new corrected request ID traverses every normal guard; no generic evidence-error exemption or compatibility path exists. The pure canonical client producer derives opaque metadata/root bindings from explicitly selected retained context and semantic intent, rejects unsupported scope combinations locally, and reuses current schema validation. It performs no I/O or authority grant; live guards remain authoritative. Semantic dismissal selects one category-specific registered action (TEXT.QUIT, UILIST.QUIT, WORLDGEN_CONFIRM.QUIT or ordinary QUIT). Only rowless POPUP_WAIT with exactly ANY_INPUT/COORDINATE excluding the pinned ubiquitous toggle_language_to_en uses one existing SPACE key; registered QUIT retains cancellation, and other missing/extra controls or rows block. Exact-image and original-phase guards remain; one input returns partial without answering a later prompt. Returned navigation into an exact same-session ordinary menu retains its verified prefix without crediting the menu-opening step; explicit menu/editor controls share original root/Work/deadlines and costs, including recovered suffixes. Menu inspection is a zero-input menu outcome; standalone inspection remains a normal-play skill. Unknown delivery and unsupported boundaries stay stopped.

Owner: controller and viewer maintainer. Trigger: every relevant request, observation and image decode.
Enforcement: Implemented at runtime; regression execution is C-PORTABLE. Source references alone establish no behavioral pass.
Failure response: Reject or freeze further dispatch; expose error and reconcile by observation before explicit resume.

### C-BOUNDARY — Architectural dependency contracts (automatic)

Declared controller and server dependency boundaries, including indirect imports through harness modules. All passive gameplay modules, including supervision, must not import controller, HTTP, CLI or process/build tooling. Shared movement policy cannot depend on consumers, clock, filesystem or transport. Import Linter uses the pyproject.toml forbidden contracts: controller cannot depend on server, CLI, declared network modules or build tooling; server cannot depend on CLI/tools; CLI may compose both. Fourth forbidden contract isolates harness.movement; negative import fixtures exercise it.

Owner: harness maintainer. Trigger: common command; architecture changes require rule review.
Enforcement: Common command runs the real lint-imports executable and propagates failure; temporary source fixtures exercise allowed composition and direct/indirect forbidden imports.
Failure response: Remove reversed dependency or review the boundary and checker together before accepting changed architecture.

### C-REVIEW — Design and independent change review (manual)

Consequential designs, implementation, tests, delegation and exceptions. Lead owns design/integration and verifies returned evidence; at most two workers use separate project-local worktrees and named disjoint paths, with shared runtime serialized; fresh-context review assesses contracts, risk and maintainability before acceptance. Review new or expanded custom infrastructure across code/docs/workflow/controls against S-CODE: name the existing option, unmet gap, smallest scope, owner/cost and retirement trigger; reject unjustified duplication. Before publication, inspect explicit Git author/committer identities and all new commit messages, including co-author trailers, under S-WORK. Use repository-local Git identity configuration. Before merging a PR whose Issue completion awaits merged-main validation, read gh pr view --json closingIssuesReferences, require an empty list and re-read after removing references. Prose negation is not a parser control; use GitHub computed data, no custom keyword parser. For source-dependent consequential claims, inspect executable predicates, caller cadence, units and defaults against actual outcomes; preserve mistaken rationale and which actions preceded correction. For changed native boundaries, compare synthetic category/action/row/transition assumptions with the pinned producer and retained visible frames; reject fictional UI labels used to arm control state. Reuse the existing regression/native lanes; do not infer native support from passing mocks. Development-first delivery places cohesive independent implementation/test/evidence review at integration/acceptance; consequential new boundaries retain earlier design/risk review. No routine readiness reviewer or per-action critic is added to ordinary development play. A complete unchanged unassisted development run can support its prospective functional outcome after exact-source checks/review; it is never retroactively relabeled held-out evidence. Review selection follows the decision-and-risk guidance in docs/project-management.md: choose applicable product/player/observer/architecture/research perspectives rather than every lens for every change. For consequential input/memory/learning/autonomy changes, verify the prior-document and research crosswalk required by S-ARCH, including conflicts and transfer limits. Independent proxy review does not establish real-user usability or semantic truth; no new automated semantic checker is added. For agent/memory changes, check S-ARCH's active/background ownership, automatic-versus-model feedback, attribution and revisable-advice boundaries; gameplay independence review checks that routine reasoning/curation does not depend on the engineering lead. This adds no per-action approval. At meaningful discussion/research/review/delivery checkpoints, check S-WORK action-item dispositions in the existing Issues/Project and applicable updates to authoritative principles, standards, controls and guidance; proposals and filed findings are not completed behavior. Apply S-ARCH/S-CODE generality and CDDA-class portability requirements: challenge task/menu-specific assumptions that obstruct ordinary input, inspect whole-loop recovery and changing-interface evidence, and separate shared responsibilities from game bindings. Record remaining coupling and actual portability limits. This is integration review, not a per-action gameplay gate.

Owner: lead; reviewer supplies independent findings. Trigger: significant change, new boundary/guarantee/dependency or integration checkpoint.
Enforcement: Required by S-AGENT and the GitHub work/PR workflow; independent agent review is manually recorded, not an independent GitHub human approval. Hosted enforcement is recorded separately in acceptance.
Failure response: Resolve material findings or record scoped owner/reason/revisit exception; after two unsuccessful worker repairs lead takes back the work.

### C-GOVERNANCE — Registry, evidence schema and map validation (automatic)

Standard mappings, control lifecycle/maintenance, document stewardship, local references, curated manifest metadata and generated map. Existing jsonschema validates records and YAML metadata parsed by python-frontmatter; project checks enforce current lifecycle relationships, safe references, active-only mappings, due dates, protocol source agreement and generated-map freshness. --as-of explicitly forecasts maintenance; the common command evaluates today.

Owner: maintainer. Trigger: common command; regenerate map after registry change.

### C-RELEASE — Exact candidate and evidence review (manual)

Development checkpoint provenance and formal acceptance/release source identity and validation lanes. Inspect staged diff and public identity before each checkpoint; fast structural and applicable focused tests support a frozen finite development run. Before formal acceptance/merge, resolve independent review, verify full portable/exact PR CI, pins/exceptions and relevant native/graphical outcomes. A complete unchanged development run may supply prospective functional evidence after qualification, without becoming held-out data. Git owns source identity: commit before each native run, use commit/tree/diff/PR and hash external artifacts rather than building source history.

Owner: lead or releasing maintainer. Trigger: Development source checkpoint; comprehensive qualification at integrated acceptance, merge, release or new support claim.
Enforcement: Main requires a PR, the Actions-bound controller check and resolved conversations; no force-push/deletion or configured bypass. Lead still owns native/release acceptance. Zero required human approvals is an explicit single-account limit; agent review is not human approval.
Failure response: Block affected development on applicable authority/identity/Pause/budget/delivery/migration/cleanup failures. Hold formal acceptance/release until required failed or unexecuted lanes are resolved; preserve original outcomes and limits. Pending unrelated full CI is not an automatic development gate.

### C-MAINTENANCE — Drift, recovery and retention review (manual)

Active guidance, dependency/research freshness, failure evidence and project-owned cleanup. Review active guidance/visuals, controls and dependencies on changed behavior/failure/release/resumption and within recorded periodic dates. Record findings, effectiveness, cost and follow-up in registry with dated evidence; promote repeated defects into tests or revise/retire controls. C-GOVERNANCE detects elapsed due dates when invoked. Revisit custom tools/processes and rejected reuse choices on upstream support/capability, requirement, defect or upkeep changes; replace or retire duplication under the existing owner/record. At meaningful integration/closeout checkpoints compare useful gameplay reached with available verification/review/waiting time, recurring failures, escaped regressions and interventions. Simplify costly low-yield steps or strengthen targeted checks from evidence; do not create a new tracker, scheduler or arbitrary numerical quota.

Owner: maintainer; lead tracks active work. Trigger: behavior/control failure, release, resumed work or active-development review interval.
Enforcement: Manual requirements under S-OPS/S-AGENT/S-DOCS/S-EVIDENCE, with registry fields, references and overdue dates enforced by C-GOVERNANCE in the common lane.
Failure response: Record specific owner and next action, repair inaccurate guidance and preserve unresolved failures; never delete saves as routine cleanup.

## Interpreting results

Run `.venv/bin/python tools/check.py` for the portable lane; update this map with
`.venv/bin/python tools/governance.py --write`. The latter validates before writing and
does not run gameplay. Dated executions belong in [acceptance](acceptance/2026-10-17-mvp.md)
and [work](work.md), with exact candidate, failures and unexecuted lanes.
